title: Host pipeline rework: adaptive kernel prewarmer and priority worker shaping to cut prefill/decode overhead
creator: Marco Li
description: Motivation: customer-facing latency spikes during cold-start and bursty prefill workloads are dominated by host-side work: kernel probe latency, threadpool contention when multiple small requests converge, and redundant buffer staging for attention KV. Goal: reduce median and tail host overhead for prefill+decode by ~25% across mixed small/large prompt mixes without changing model weights or increasing GPU memory footprint. Approach: implement a lightweight adaptive kernel prewarmer, introduce a token-priority-aware worker pool, and replace fixed pinned-buffer staging with staged ephemeral pinning to reduce syscalls.
acceptance_criteria: Median host overhead (prefill+decode) reduced by >=20% on ci/latency-bench-smallprompts
P99 host overhead reduced by >=15% on bursty workload (1000rps, 1-8 tokens)
No regression in throughput on large-batch steady-state runs
Automated canary shows <1% request error increase and no GPU OOMs over 24h
work_items: Design and implement adaptive kernel prewarmer that probes common kernel variants lazily and reuses warmed cuBLAS/cuDNN kernels across sequence-length buckets
Add token-priority-aware scheduling to host threadpool: separate fast-path workers for short prefill/decode requests and pooled workers for long-running requests
Implement staged ephemeral pinning for small KV slices to avoid long-lived pinned buffer saturation and reduce page-lock syscalls
Integrate prewarmer with existing kernel-hint metadata and runtime telemetry to auto-tune probe budget per model
Measure and add perf regression checks to CI and console dashboard; create canary rollout with traffic shaping
comments: 2026-03-02 by Marco Li: Spike completed on kernel prewarmer prototype. Warmup times dropped ~60% for small sequence lengths on devbox (A100). Added microbench harness in github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/prewarm-probe
2026-03-04 by Aisha Raman: Scoped worker pool change to non-intrusive switch gated by runtime flag. Need E2E tests for mixed-size request bursts before enabling by default.
2026-03-06 by Jin Park (review): Reviewed prewarmer code. Suggest limiting probe concurrency to avoid queuing on memcpy path. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2845
2026-03-08 by Priya Das (SRE): Observability hooks added. Please ensure we emit probe-rate metrics and per-worker queue latency to console for rollout monitoring.

2026-03-10 by Aisha Raman: Integrated ephemeral pinning. End-to-end tests show reduced page-lock syscalls in perf trace. Still seeing ~8% contention on worker mutex under synthetic 2k rps; investigating adaptive backoff.
2026-03-12 by Marco Li: Canary started on staging-3 with 5% traffic. Initial 12h telemetry: median host overhead -22%, p99 -13%, no errors. Plan to ramp to 20% next week pending second safety run.
timeline: Week 1: prototype prewarmer and microbench. Week 2: implement worker shaping and ephemeral pinning + unit tests. Week 3: integrate telemetry, run staging canary, iterate on backoff. Week 4: rollout to 20% then 100% if safe.
